Summary: The vertex linear arboricity \(vla(G)\) of a graph \(G\) is the minimum number of subsets into which the vertex set \(V(G)\) can be partitioned so that each subset induces a subgraph whose connected components are paths. In this paper, we seek to convert vertex linear arboricity into its fractional analogues, i.e., the fractional vertex linear arboricity of graphs. Let \(Z_n\) denote the additive group of integers modulo \(n\). Suppose that \(C\subseteq Z_n\setminus 0\) has the additional property that it is closed under additive inverse, that is, \(-c\in C\) if and only if \(c\in C\). A circulant graph is the graph \(G(Z_n,C)\) with the vertex set \(Z_n\) and \(i\), \(j\) are adjacent if and only if \(i-j\in C\). The fractional vertex linear arboricity of the complete \(n\)-partite graph, the cycle \(C_n\), the integer distance graph \(G(D)\) for \(D=\{1,2,\dots ,m\}\), \(D=\{2,3,\dots ,m\}\) and \(D=P\) the set of all prime numbers, the Petersen graph and the circulant graph \(G_{a,b}=G(Z_a,C)\) with \(C=\{-a+b,\dots ,-b,b,\dots ,a-b\}\) \((a-2b\geq b-3\geq 3)\) are determined, and an upper and a lower bounds of the fractional vertex linear arboricity of Mycielski graph are obtained.
